correctness.rationale: PASS: The minimizer is unique by strict convexity. Each maximal constant block is a scalar p-mean. For \(p<2\) coordinate monotonicity and translation give a sharp upper \(n^{1/p}\), while \(p>2\) stationarity implies each normalized derivative weight <=1/2 and hence a sharp \((n/2)^{1/p}\) upper; the finite-selection lemma pastes block maps globally. All-pooling KKT multipliers remain positive near two explicit samples. The unique-zero perturbation proves lower \(n^{1/p}\) below two; endpoint-supported gradient proves lower \((n/2)^{1/p}\) above two. Dimension <=2 and \(p=2\) have Lip 1, attained since the projection fixes feasible data. Analytic derivations, not numerical checks, cover all real inputs and n.
